answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a stake that is slashable when independent audits show an identity was duplicated or its claims conflict with verified history. The audit links accounts through costly-to-forge credentials, while random reviewers check a ridge of evidence rather than trusting profile names. A crystal-clear appeal path limits false penalties; juniper is simply a sample account label, not proof of personhood. A sybil attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it, making mass identities expensive even if creating accounts is free.
